luke.19.p1.b1.text: Then Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through. And there was a man named Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, who was very wealthy.

luke.19.p1.b2.text: But could not see over the crowd because he was small in stature.

luke.19.p1.b3.text: So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Him,

luke.19.p2.b1.text: When Jesus came to that place, He looked up

luke.19.p2.b2.text: “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.”

luke.19.p2.b3.text: So Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed Him joyfully.

luke.19.p3.b1.text: “He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!”

luke.19.p3.b2.text: But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord,

luke.19.p3.b3.text: “Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor,

luke.19.p3.b4.text: And if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.”

luke.19.p4.b1.text: “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.

luke.19.p4.b2.text: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”

luke.19.p5.b1.text: … Jesus proceeded to tell them a parable, because He was near Jerusalem and they thought the kingdom of God would appear imminently.

luke.19.p5.b2.text: “A man of noble birth went to a distant country to lay claim to his kingship and then return. Beforehand, he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas.

luke.19.p5.b3.text: ‘Conduct business with this until I return,’

luke.19.p5.b4.text: ‘We do not want this man to rule over us.’

luke.19.p6.b1.text: When he returned from procuring his kingship, he summoned the servants to whom he had given the money, to find out what each one had earned.

luke.19.p6.b2.text: ‘Master, your mina has produced ten more minas.’

luke.19.p6.b3.text: ‘Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter, you shall have authority over ten cities.’

luke.19.p6.b4.text: ‘Master, your mina has made five minas.’

luke.19.p7.b1.text: ‘Master, here is your mina, which I have laid away in a piece of cloth.

luke.19.p7.b2.text: For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man. …

luke.19.p7.b3.text: ‘You wicked servant, I will judge you by your own words.

luke.19.p7.b4.text: Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?’

luke.19.p8.b1.text: ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’

luke.19.p8.b3.text: ‘I tell you that everyone who has will be given more; but the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

luke.19.p9.b1.text: After Jesus had said this, He went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.

luke.19.p9.b2.text: As He approached Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives,

luke.19.p9.b3.text: saying, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.

luke.19.p9.b4.text: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it.’”

luke.19.p10.b1.text: So those who were sent went out and found it just as Jesus had told them.

luke.19.p10.b4.text: Then they led the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it, and put Jesus on it.

luke.19.p11.b1.text: As He rode along, the people spread their cloaks on the road.

luke.19.p11.b2.text: And as He approached the descent from the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of disciples began to praise God joyfully in a loud voice for all the miracles they had seen:

luke.19.p11.b3.text: “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”

luke.19.p12.b2.text: “I tell you,” … “if they remain silent, the very stones will cry out.”

luke.19.p13.b1.text: As Jesus approached Jerusalem and saw the city, He wept over it

luke.19.p13.b2.text: “If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace!

luke.19.p13.b3.text: But now it is hidden from your eyes.

luke.19.p14.b1.text: For the days will come upon you when your enemies will barricade you and surround you and hem you in on every side.

luke.19.p14.b2.text: They will not leave one stone on another,

luke.19.p14.b3.text: Because you did not recognize the time of your visitation from God.”

luke.19.p15.b1.text: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were selling there.

luke.19.p15.b2.text: “It is written: ‘My house will be a house of prayer.’

luke.19.p15.b3.text: But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”

luke.19.p16.b1.text: Jesus was teaching at the temple every day,

luke.19.p16.b2.text: But the chief priests, scribes, and leaders of the people were intent on killing Him.

luke.19.p17.b1.text: Yet they could not find a way to do so,

luke.19.p17.b2.text: Because all the people hung on His words.
